target: Estou feliz porque passei na prova.
english: I'm happy because I passed the exam.
tip: Emotions triggered by events use 'estar' – you're happy now because of something that happened. It's a reaction, not your personality.

target: O que significa PF no cardápio?
english: What does PF mean on the menu?
tip: 'PF' stands for 'prato feito' – a cheap, filling meal typically including rice, beans, meat, salad, and an egg. Found in restaurants all over Brazil.

target: Os filhos deles estudam na mesma escola.
english: Their children study at the same school.
tip: 'Deles' = theirs/of them (de + eles, masculine). 'Delas' = de + elas (feminine). Used to clarify 'seu/sua' which can be ambiguous.

target: O mapa da cidade está no celular.
english: The city map is on the phone.
tip: 'Mapa' is masculine despite ending in -a: o mapa. Other exceptions: o dia, o cinema, o problema, o tema, o sistema.

target: O nome do restaurante é difícil de lembrar.
english: The restaurant's name is hard to remember.
tip: 'O nome' is masculine despite ending in -e. Some -e words are masculine: nome, leite, café.

target: A estação do metrô fica a dois quarteirões.
english: The subway station is two blocks away.
tip: 'Ficar' for permanent locations: 'o hotel fica perto' = the hotel is (located) near. More specific than 'estar.'

target: A água do rio é clara e fria.
english: The river water is clear and cold.
tip: 'De + o/a/os/as' always contracts to 'do/da/dos/das' – these contractions are mandatory, never optional.

target: Como é que eu faço para reservar?
english: How do I go about making a reservation?
tip: 'Como é que' is a very common Brazilian reinforcement of 'como.' Adding 'é que' makes questions sound more natural and conversational.

target: Ele é do Rio, mas mora em São Paulo.
english: He's from Rio, but lives in São Paulo.
tip: Origin uses 'ser' (é do Rio = permanent) while current residence can use 'morar' (mora em SP = where he currently lives).

target: O restaurante é mais caro do que eu pensava.
english: The restaurant is more expensive than I thought.
tip: Comparatives use 'mais + adjective + do que': mais caro do que = more expensive than. The 'do' is optional in speech.

target: Ele é tímido no começo, mas depois se abre.
english: He's shy at first, but opens up later.
tip: 'Em + o/a/os/as' contracts to 'no/na/nos/nas' – always use the contracted form.

target: Vou ao banco pagar as contas.
english: I'm going to the bank to pay the bills.
tip: 'Ao' is the contraction of 'a + o' (to the, masculine). 'Vou ao banco' = I go to the bank.

target: Minha mãe é baiana, nasceu em Salvador.
english: My mom is Bahian, she was born in Salvador.
tip: Origin and birthplace are permanent – always use 'ser.' 'É baiana' = she is Bahian (forever).

target: Esse restaurante é tão bom quanto caro.
english: This restaurant is as good as it is expensive.
tip: Contractions with 'aqui/ali/aquilo': de+aqui=daqui (from here), de+ali=dali (from there) – common in everyday speech.

target: O apartamento novo é maior que o antigo.
english: The new apartment is bigger than the old one.
tip: 'Maior' means bigger/larger. It's an irregular comparative – you don't say 'mais grande.' Similarly: menor (smaller), melhor (better), pior (worse).

target: O que aconteceu?
english: What happened?
tip: 'O que' = what. 'Acontecer' means 'to happen.' Past tense here: 'aconteceu' (pretérito perfeito).

target: Onde é a saída?
english: Where's the exit?
tip: 'Onde é' = where is (permanent location). Use 'onde é' for places, 'onde está' for movable things.

target: Quem é aquele cara?
english: Who's that guy?
tip: 'Cara' is informal Brazilian Portuguese for 'guy/dude.' Very common in everyday speech.

target: Qual é o seu nome?
english: What's your name?
tip: 'Qual' means 'which/what' when choosing from options or asking for specific information. 'Qual é o seu nome?' is the standard way to ask someone's name.

target: Quando você chega?
english: When do you arrive?
tip: 'Quando' = when. Portuguese questions often keep statement word order: 'Quando você chega?' not 'Quando chega você?'

target: Onde você mora?
english: Where do you live?
tip: 'Onde' = where. 'Morar' means 'to live/reside.' 'Onde você mora?' is one of the most common questions.

target: Falou, até depois!
english: Alright, see you later!
tip: 'Falou' (literally 'spoke') is a casual goodbye in Brazil, like 'later' or 'peace out.' Often combined: 'falou, valeu!'

target: Quem é aquela pessoa?
english: Who is that person?
tip: 'Quem' = who. 'Aquela' is the feminine demonstrative for 'that (over there).' 'Aquele' for masculine.

target: Quem fez esse bolo?
english: Who made this cake?
tip: 'Quem' as subject: 'Quem fez?' = Who made? The verb agrees with the implied subject (third person singular).

target: Quando vocês se mudaram?
english: When did you move?
tip: 'Quando vocês se mudaram?' – 'mudar-se' is reflexive: to move (house). 'Mudar' alone = to change.

target: Por que vocês estão rindo?
english: Why are you laughing?
tip: 'Por que' (two words) is used in questions. 'Porque' (one word) is for answers. This is one of the trickiest spelling rules in Portuguese.

target: Quando é o seu aniversário?
english: When is your birthday?
tip: 'Quando é' = when is. 'Aniversário' is used for both birthday and anniversary in Portuguese.

target: Por que você está triste?
english: Why are you sad?
tip: 'Por que' + estar for temporary states: 'Por que você está triste?' uses 'estar' because moods are temporary.

target: Quem é o responsável aqui?
english: Who's in charge here?
tip: 'Quem é o responsável' = who is in charge. Useful in work and service situations.

target: O que você está lendo?
english: What are you reading?
tip: `estar + gerúndio` = English '-ing right now': `estou comendo` = 'I'm eating'. Brazilians use this way more than Spanish/Italian use their gerundios.

target: Qual é a senha do Wi-Fi?
english: What's the Wi-Fi password?
tip: 'Qual é a senha' = what's the password. 'Senha' means password, PIN, or queue number in Brazil.

target: Qual é a sua cor favorita?
english: What's your favorite color?
tip: 'Qual' = which/what. 'Qual é o seu nome?' is more common than 'Como é o seu nome?'

target: Quando você volta?
english: When are you coming back?
tip: 'Quando você volta?' – 'Voltar' = to come back/return. Present tense used for near future plans.

target: Quando a reunião começa?
english: When does the meeting start?
tip: 'Quando' + present tense for scheduled events: 'Quando a reunião começa?' = When does the meeting start?

target: Como você veio para cá?
english: How did you get here?
tip: 'Como' asking about manner/method: 'Como você veio?' = How did you come? Expects a method answer.

target: Onde a gente se encontra?
english: Where do we meet up?
tip: 'Onde a gente se encontra?' – reflexive 'se encontrar' = to meet up. 'A gente' = we (informal).

target: Por que o voo atrasou?
english: Why was the flight delayed?
tip: 'Por que' for asking reasons about events: 'Por que o voo atrasou?' = Why was the flight delayed?

target: O que significa essa palavra?
english: What does this word mean?
tip: 'O que significa' = what does it mean. Very useful for language learners! 'Essa' = this (feminine).

target: Eu gosto do clima daqui.
english: I like the weather here.
tip: 'Daqui' = de + aqui (from here). Similar contractions: dali (de + ali), daí (de + aí), daquele (de + aquele).

target: O dia está lindo hoje.
english: The day is beautiful today.
tip: 'Dia' is masculine (o dia) despite ending in -a. It's one of the most common exceptions to the gender rule.

target: Quando a gente pode se mudar?
english: When can we move in?
tip: 'Quando' = when. Portuguese questions don't require inverted punctuation like Spanish's ¿?

target: A sala de espera está lotada.
english: The waiting room is packed.
tip: Portuguese articles contract with prepositions: de+o=do, em+a=na, a+a=à. These are never optional.

target: A qualidade dos produtos é boa.
english: The product quality is good.
tip: 'dos' contracts de+os – mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Eu gosto de cozinhar para os amigos.
english: I like cooking for friends.
tip: 'Gostar de' + infinitive: 'gosto de cozinhar.' 'Para os amigos' = for friends. Purpose with 'para.'

target: Os vizinhos do andar de cima são barulhentos.
english: The upstairs neighbors are noisy.
tip: 'vizinhos' – diminutive suffix expressing smallness, affection, or informality, not just physical size.

target: Como ficou o bolo?
english: How did the cake turn out?
tip: 'Ficar' is used to describe how something turned out or ended up. 'Como ficou?' = How did it come out?

target: Bom dia! Dormiu bem?
english: Good morning! Did you sleep well?
tip: Regular -er/-ir verbs: the eu form in the preterite ends in -i, the ele/ela form in -eu/-iu.

target: Como funciona o metrô daqui?
english: How does the subway work here?
tip: 'Como' = how. 'Funcionar' = to work/function. 'Daqui' = de + aqui = from here/around here.

target: O que você vai querer?
english: What are you going to have?
tip: 'O que' for 'what' in questions about things. 'Vai querer' = will want – near future with 'ir + infinitive.'

target: Quem vai levar as crianças?
english: Who's going to take the kids?
tip: 'Quem vai' = who will. 'Levar' = to take (someone somewhere). 'Buscar' = to pick up (the opposite).

target: O livro está na estante.
english: The book is on the shelf.
tip: 'O' is the masculine definite article. Most nouns ending in -o are masculine: o livro, o carro, o gato.

target: Eu moro no centro da cidade.
english: I live in the city center.
tip: 'No' is the contraction of 'em + o' (in the, masculine). 'Na' is 'em + a' (in the, feminine). Both are mandatory.

target: O pai dele trabalha no hospital.
english: His dad works at the hospital.
tip: 'O pai' = the father. Family terms change gender: pai/mãe, filho/filha, irmão/irmã.

target: A noite está agradável para caminhar.
english: The evening is pleasant for walking.
tip: 'Noite' is feminine: a noite. Time periods: a manhã (morning), a tarde (afternoon), a noite (night). All feminine.

target: A casa dela fica perto do parque.
english: Her house is near the park.
tip: 'A' is the feminine definite article. Most nouns ending in -a are feminine: a casa, a mesa, a porta.

target: O ônibus dos alunos chega às sete.
english: The students' bus arrives at seven.
tip: 'Dos' is the contraction of 'de + os' (of the, masculine plural). 'Das' = 'de + as' (feminine plural).

target: Os gatos da vizinha são muito barulhentos.
english: The neighbor's cats are very noisy.
tip: `-inho` softens tone: `um momentinho` (just a sec), `obrigadinho` (thanks, friendly). Not about size – about warmth.

target: O porteiro do prédio é muito prestativo.
english: The building doorman is very helpful.
tip: 'Porteiro' is a very common figure in Brazilian apartments – the doorman/concierge who manages building access.

target: Eu preciso de ajuda com essa mudança.
english: I need help with this move.
tip: 'Precisar de' means 'to need.' The 'de' is required: 'preciso de ajuda,' not 'preciso ajuda.' However, before infinitives, many Brazilians drop the 'de.'

target: Vamos aos correios amanhã.
english: Let's go to the post office tomorrow.
tip: 'Aos' is the contraction of 'a + os' (to the, masculine plural). 'Às' = 'a + as' (feminine plural).
